title: Forward reservation scenarios and per-contract allocation table Q2 2029
description: Working spreadsheet with alternative reservation scenarios for Dedicated customers, focused on multi-region GPU allocations, burst envelopes, and fallback tiers for Q2 planning.
summary: This sheet captures three forward-looking reservation scenarios and a per-contract allocation table to help SRE/Infra and Sales Ops coordinate capacity commitments for Dedicated customers. It emphasizes region pinning, allowed burst windows, utilization forecasts, and automated fallback policies for constrained supply.
assumptions: Base fleet adds 120 A100-equivalent cards across us-west, eu-central, and ap-south between Apr 1 and May 15, 2029.
Average committed utilization target = 62% sustained over monthly windows; acceptable peak bursting up to 95% for short events.
Quantization/optimized kernels reduce token cost for some customers but do not change physical GPU entitlements.
SLA tiers require 99.9% availability for dedicated pools; regional outages trigger cross-region failover with 20% degraded throughput.
Customers are allowed configurable burst budgets (5–20% of committed slices) subject to global capacity state.

scenarios: Optimistic supply: All scheduled hardware arrivals complete on time; enable graduated overcommit up to 10% for short bursts; expected global utilization settles at 60%.
Constrained supply: 30% of Q2 capacity delayed due to HW procurement; enforce strict burst gating, promote model-quantization recommendations, and start momentary throttles for low-tier customers.
Regional outage (eu-central): Shift eu-central commitments to secondary regions; priority routing preserves 70% of throughput for enterprise SLA contracts with increased cost allocation.

High-burst event (marketing launch): Multiple customers request full burst simultaneously for 48 hours; temporarily throttle non-committed trial customers and enact emergency burst budget rebalancing policy.
allocation_rules: Rule 1: Commitments are allocated by region_priority; if primary region capacity < committed_gpus, attempt secondary region within 30 minutes.
Rule 2: Burst allowance is consumed first from local pool, then from global overflow; deny bursts when global utilization > 88%.
Rule 3: Customers flagged 'enterprise-sla' cannot be evicted for bursting except in declared regional emergency with cross-region fallback engaged.
Rule 4: Overcommit ceiling = min(10% of physical GPUs, sum of allowed_burst across active contracts) and evaluated daily at 02:00 UTC.
Rule 5: Quantization-enabled deployments get prioritized placement on mixed-precision nodes to improve unit economics but do not change hard GPU entitlement.
utilization_forecast_notes: Weekly rolling forecast generated from per-contract telemetry + sales pipeline. Current model projects two distinct peaks: product launches in Apr and May; steady state in Jun. Forecast accuracy historically +/- 7% per month.
